toolRuntime.typeHint: How the ontology action executor calls this tool: echo returns the inputs (for testing); API calls a regular HTTP endpoint; None means no callable entry (execution returns no_runtime)
toolRuntime.urlHint: Use {param} placeholders in the path; values come from tool inputs and are URL-encoded. Placeholders are not allowed in the host
toolRuntime.urlInvalid: URL must start with http:// or https:// and the host must not contain {param}
toolRuntime.queryHint: Like {"name": "value or {param}"}; a parameter whose whole value is one {param} is skipped when that input is empty. If omitted, GET / DELETE send the inputs as query parameters
toolRuntime.headersHint: Fixed headers. Authorization and Cookie cannot be set here; use the authentication settings below for credentials
toolRuntime.bodyHint: A value that is exactly {param} keeps the input's type; partial placeholders are joined as strings; keys whose value is empty are dropped. If omitted, all inputs are sent as the JSON body
toolRuntime.secretHint: Stored encrypted and never shown again after saving
toolRuntime.secretKeepHint: A credential is set. Leave empty to keep it; enter a new value to replace it
toolRuntime.extractHint: Like {"status": "$.data.status"}: pick fields from the JSON response with dot paths ([index] supported). If omitted, the response is returned as is
toolRuntime.timeoutHint: Leave empty for the default 10 s, max {{max}} s
toolRuntime.securityHint: The URL is checked on save and on every call: it must not point to private, loopback or link-local addresses, and redirects are not followed. Internal endpoints need ops to add the host to the ONTOLOGY_TOOL_RUNTIME_ALLOWED_HOSTS allowlist.
toolRuntime.jsonBodyInvalid: Must be a JSON object or array
toolRuntime.mockHint: For testing: look up a table by one input. Like {"by": "input name", "rows": {"input value": {data}}, "default": {data when not found}}; the result goes to the output's data field. If omitted, only the inputs are echoed
toolRuntime.readOnlyCheckbox: This endpoint only reads data and never changes anything in the target system
toolRuntime.readOnlyHint: You declare this explicitly; it is not inferred from the method (GET does not mean read-only). Only read-only tools can be called automatically by knowledge base Q&A. Unchecked tools are treated as write operations.
